claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard NIST P-256 generator P, the Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md with the negation map recovers x with probability at least 0.544 (hence at least 0.39) at the stated mean step budget, with expected total work at most 2^128.724770 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification, under the disclosed random-walk heuristic of proof.md Section 4. Peak memory is at most 2^103.42 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^15.0 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. This is an analytic argument, not a claim of practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check the Pollard rho walk logic with the negation map, distinguished points, cycle detection with restart, and collision resolution on a small additive cyclic group. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: p256-ecdlp: Pollard rho with the negation map
